# Parity: pandas == SQL

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/nf/gen_cookbook.py from tests/parity/test_parity.py. Do not edit by hand. -->

Is the SQL rule the same as its pandas twin? This page answers that for every one of the 77 rules, straight from the parity test
([`tests/parity/test_parity.py`](https://github.com/bbartling/open-fdd/blob/master/tests/parity/test_parity.py)), so it changes when the test changes.

| | Rules |
|---|---:|
| SQL rules | **77** |
| With a pandas twin | **71** |
| Match on the synthetic suite | **46** |
| Known divergence (documented below) | **25** |
| SQL only (no twin) | **6** |

## What "match" means

The suite builds a deterministic SI dataset (`AHU-1` mostly healthy, `AHU-2` with injected fault windows; three days on a 5-minute grid) and runs
it through the SQL pack on PGlite (real PostgreSQL) and SQLite, and through the pandas rules. A rule **matches** when its confirmed fault hours agree
to 1e-6 h on every equipment. The two SQL engines must agree with each other on all 77 rules. The test fails in both directions: a rule that starts
to diverge, or one that starts to match, has to be moved in the table below, so this page cannot go stale. Matching on this dataset is strong
evidence, not a proof for every possible input.

## Why 25 of 71 differ

**Not units.** Every value on both sides is SI and the threshold equations were checked to use the same constants. The differences are in **how the rule
decides the equipment is "on" (the gate), how it proves cooling or heating (the proof), how weather is joined, or how many samples it holds after a mode
change**. Two rules differ for their own reasons: `SV-RATE` is a different algorithm and `TRIM-4` treats missing inputs differently.


- **9 rules**: SQL and pandas gate 'equipment on' with different fan/pump proof order and thresholds. (`AHU-SATDEV`, `CHW-2`, `FC13-SAT-HIGH`, `FC14`, `FC6`, `FC7`, `FCU-HTG-COIL`, `HP-1`, `TRIM-1`)
- **9 rules**: SQL holds the fan-restart / mode-delay window over rolling rows, pandas GL36 suppresses after a mode change: differs by a few samples at fault edges. (`AHU-SIMUL`, `CHW-1`, `ECON-4`, `FC5`, `FCU-MODE-CYCLE`, `FCU-VALVE-PASS-CLG`, `OA-1`, `VAV-6`, `VAV-AHU-LEAVE`)
- **3 rules**: weather source: SQL prefers equipment web_oa_* then as-of weather rows; pandas resolves its own web columns. (`ECON-3`, `ECON-7`, `OAT-METEO`)
- **2 rules**: pandas proves equipment/cooling from typed roles (mechanical_proof_mask, equipment_type); SQL ORs chiller status / valve. (`CHW-NOLOAD-1`, `MECH-OAT-1`)
- **1 rule**: documented in sql/fdd/KNOWN_DIFFERENCES.md: pandas uses profile/median/persistence logic, SQL two consecutive exceedances. (`SV-RATE`)
- **1 rule**: pandas skips (missing roles: reset requests); SQL treats absent requests as zero. (`TRIM-4`)

Closing a gap means making one side adopt the other's definition (for example, SQL adopting the pandas mechanical-proof order) and removing the
rule from `KNOWN_DIVERGENT`. Until then the SQL result is the production result and the pandas twin is the notebook reference; read the reason column
before comparing numbers between them. Other known differences: [`sql/fdd/KNOWN_DIFFERENCES.md`](https://github.com/bbartling/open-fdd/blob/master/sql/fdd/KNOWN_DIFFERENCES.md).

## Parameter default differences

Shared parameter keys whose SI default differs between the pandas rule and the SQL catalog (none of them is a unit problem). `test_pandas_defaults_equal_sql_catalog` pins temperature, flow and pressure defaults; these are fraction/hour/signal-span keys outside that check.

| Rule | Parameter | pandas default | SQL default |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| [FC13-SAT-HIGH](sql-cookbook.html#fc13-sat-high) | `clg_full_min` | 0.01 | 0.9 |
| [FC14](sql-cookbook.html#fc14) | `clg_inactive_max` | 0.1 | 0.01 |
| [FC15](sql-cookbook.html#fc15) | `clg_inactive_max` | 0.1 | 0.01 |
| [SV-RATE](sql-cookbook.html#sv-rate) | `max_gap_hours` | 2 | 1 |
| [SV-RATE](sql-cookbook.html#sv-rate) | `sensor_span` | 0 | 100 |
